Triggers.value: A memory of the event coming to mind suddenly

Threat.value: I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people
Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place

Memory.value: The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things
Remembering what happened during the frightening event is just like looking at photographs of it in my mind.

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel like I don't know myself anymore
I can't deal with even the slightest upset
The event happened because of the way I acted

vignette: Emma, a 26-year-old European American firefighter, has been struggling to come to terms with her traumatic experience of captivity. Despite her strong will and resilience in the face of danger, she finds herself haunted by vivid memories that seem almost too real. The event that left Emma so shaken occurred while she was on duty at an apartment complex fire. She was trapped for hours in a burning building, surrounded by smoke and flames. The memory is seared into her mind, more real than any ordinary recollection; it feels like looking through photographs of the ordeal every time it surfaces. This photographic recall intensifies her distress because each detail feels incredibly vivid and alienating, as if the experience belonged to someone else. Emma's triggers have become a constant source of unease in her daily life. Old photos from that time can instantly transport her back to those frightening moments, making her feel like she's reliving it all over again. This intrusion is particularly troubling for Emma because she has come to believe that she doesn't know herself anymore-her sense of identity feels lost amidst these intrusive memories. Crowded spaces at the fire station also trigger intense flashbacks and startle responses. She jumps at ordinary sounds, like a pager going off or sirens in the distance, which reinforces her belief that she can't cope with any kind of upset. This self-blame adds to her emotional burden, as she feels responsible for the traumatic event and cannot relax even when she knows she is safe. The memory of captivity becomes more intense whenever Emma encounters a trigger, leading to a vicious cycle where these intrusive memories fuel her sense of threat. She startsle easily at sudden sounds, which in turn heightens her flashbacks and keeps her from relaxing. Her belief that she can't cope exacerbates the fear, making each sound and memory more distressing. Emma's job as a firefighter is particularly challenging because it puts her in situations where triggers are unavoidable. Crowded spaces during training drills or emergency calls often lead to intense memories of captivity, further cementing her negative appraisals. She has become increasingly isolated at work, avoiding interactions that might remind her of the trauma and heighten her sense of threat. The loop tightens as Emma's memory and threat responses become more intertwined. Her intrusive thoughts are both a cause and consequence of her heightened sense of danger. Every time she feels threatened by a sound or crowded space, it triggers another vivid flashback, reinforcing her belief that she is not in control and cannot cope with the simplest upsets. What finally brought Emma to seek help was an incident where she had a severe panic attack during a fire call. She felt like she couldn't function effectively and feared endangering others. This realization made her acutely aware of how much she has changed since the event-she no longer feels like herself, and the constant fear and self-blame are overwhelming. Emma is now seeking help to regain control over her life and work. She hopes to find ways to manage her symptoms so that she can continue to serve as a firefighter without being consumed by her traumatic memories. Her deepest fear is losing her identity completely and becoming someone who cannot handle even the simplest challenges, but with therapy, she believes she can reclaim her sense of self and regain control over her life.
